sections.h2: Where is Parkersburg, WV, and how did it grow?
sections.html:
Parkersburg is the seat of Wood County and sits where the Little Kanawha River meets the Ohio River. Wikipedia lists the 2020 census population at 29,738, which ranks it fourth in the state, and the Parkersburg and Vienna metro area at 89,490.

Settlers first called the town Newport. Land had been granted to Alexander Parker for Revolutionary War service, a title dispute with the town planners was settled in 1809 in favor of his heirs, and the town took the name Parkersburg in 1810. It was chartered in 1820 and rechartered as a city in 1860.

The Baltimore and Ohio Railroad built a branch line south from Wheeling in 1857 and a railroad bridge to Belpre, Ohio between 1868 and 1870. The city covers about 12.35 square miles, of which 11.82 are land.

The Little Kanawha divides the city into a north side and a south side. South Parkersburg was a separate city until it joined Parkersburg in 1950.

sections.h2: Which Parkersburg neighborhoods do sellers hear about most?
sections.html:
The north end holds most of the named neighborhoods, and each has a different housing style. Wikipedia lists these areas on the north side:

  • Downtown, Julia-Ann Square and Quincy Hill
  • Beechwood, Fairview Heights and Granada Hills
  • Meadowcrest, Oakwood Estates and Woodland Park
  • Riverside, Worthington and the East End

South of the river, the former city of South Parkersburg is joined by suburban areas of southern Wood County, including Blennerhassett, Lubeck and Washington to the southwest and Mineral Wells to the southeast. Some of those sit outside the city, so tax and code rules differ by address.

Which part of town your house falls into can affect flood zone status, which the next section covers.

sections.h2: What is the Parkersburg floodwall, and does it affect my house?
sections.html:
The Parkersburg Floodwall protects low lying parts of the city along the Ohio and Little Kanawha rivers, and owners inside the protected zone pay a maintenance fee. The city code, in Article 783, defines the protected flood zone as all properties at or below an average of 624 feet above sea level that the floodwall protects. The City Engineer determines the boundaries. You can read the definitions in the city's codified ordinances.

The code declares that owners of property in the flood zone are the users and beneficiaries of the floodwall and bear the cost of its continuance, maintenance and improvement. Article 783 also sets a payment schedule and penalties and is administered by the city's Director of Finance. A Parkersburg Flood Wall Board is established separately in the administrative code.

ItemWhat the city code says
Protected flood zoneProperties at or below about 624 feet above sea level, protected by the floodwall
Who sets the boundaryThe City Engineer
Who pays maintenance feesOwners of property in the zone
Who administers itDirector of Finance
Residential buildingDefined to exclude rentals of four or more units on one tract

If you are selling inside that zone, find out whether any floodwall fees are unpaid, because the code includes penalties. A title company can also confirm whether a balance affects the closing. Anyone can check a specific address on the state's flood map tool.

sections.h2: How does code enforcement work for a vacant or neglected house in Parkersburg?
sections.html:
The city's Code Enforcement Division is the enforcement arm for building, health and safety, zoning and nuisance codes. Its stated goal is voluntary compliance from property and business owners, and it takes further steps where that fails. The division's page describes this approach.

A separate body, the Building Enforcement Agency, meets monthly. The city's boards page says it meets on the first Monday of each month at 9:00 a.m. and includes the Mayor, the City Engineer and the Code Enforcement Director. The city says the agency works to address neglected, vacant and abandoned properties, which it describes as critical to the stability of residents, small businesses and the community.

State law supports this work. West Virginia Code section 8-12-16c gives a municipality authority to create a vacant building and property registration and maintenance program by ordinance.

  • Keep grass and exterior debris under control while a house sits empty.
  • Respond to any notice from the division in writing and keep a copy.
  • Ask the division about open complaints before you sign a sale contract.

An owner who inherits a neglected house and cannot afford repairs may find a direct sale simpler than going through a repair schedule. Cash Home Buyers looks at each Parkersburg property as is, with no obligation if you decline an offer.

sections.h2: What drives the Parkersburg economy and who buys homes here?
sections.html:
Parkersburg's economy mixes chemicals, finance and federal government work. The city's economy page names DuPont, Highmark, United Bank and Woodcraft among the well known companies, and says the U.S. Treasury's Bureau of the Fiscal Service employs more than 2,000 local people.

Population has declined in each census since 1960, when it was 44,797, falling to 29,738 in 2020. The city had 13,119 households and 15,246 housing units in 2020 according to Wikipedia's census summary, about 2,100 more housing units than households.

Education adds demand. West Virginia University at Parkersburg is a public college on the outskirts of the city, and the city has three high schools: Parkersburg High, Parkersburg South and Parkersburg Catholic. Public schools are run by Wood County Schools, which also operates the Wood County Technical Center and the Caperton Center for Applied Technology.

Chemical plant, bank, federal and college jobs bring people in and out of the area, and that turnover is part of why homes change hands here.

sections.h2: How do taxes work for a Parkersburg property?
sections.html:
Wood County assesses and taxes Parkersburg property, and real estate taxes are paid at the Wood County Sheriff's office, not the Assessor. The Wood County Assessor's page says property is assessed July 1 and that your tax bill multiplies a levy rate by your assessed value, which is 60 percent of market value. Levy rates are set by the legislature for the Board of Education, the county commission and the municipalities.

The assessor's FAQ flags two points that surprise owners:

  • A home deeded to an LLC cannot be taxed as Class 2 residential property, so all LLC owned property is taxed as Class 3 or 4.
  • Only an owner occupied home with the owner's name on the deed can have Class 2 status, so a relative living in another home you own does not qualify.

State dates apply: bills issue on or after July 15, the first half is due September 1 and the second half March 1, with a 2.5 percent discount for early payment and 9 percent annual interest on delinquent amounts. See the Tax Division page.

When you sell, the transfer excise tax under section 11-22-2 is $1.10 per $500 of value, plus a county excise tax of 55 cents per $500 that counties can raise. The seller normally pays it, and a $20 fee goes to the state Affordable Housing Fund.

sections.h2: How do roads, rail and the airport connect Parkersburg?
sections.html:
Interstate 77 and US 50 are the two major highways, and WV routes 2, 14, 47, 68, 95 and 618 also pass through the city. The Mid-Ohio Valley Regional Airport had three flights a day on weekdays from Charlotte, per Wikipedia. Passenger trains stopped in the 1960s, with Amtrak's Shenandoah running from 1976 to 1981, and CSX still provides freight service.

These links matter to out of town heirs, who often need to handle a sale from a distance. A remote closing with a title company can be arranged if you cannot travel.

faqs.q: Does the Parkersburg floodwall fee affect my sale?
faqs.a: It can if your property is inside the protected flood zone. Article 783 of the city code assigns the maintenance cost to those owners and sets penalties. Ask the city's finance office whether anything is unpaid before closing.

faqs.q: Who do I call about code problems on a vacant Parkersburg house?
faqs.a: The city's Building and Code Enforcement department handles building, health and safety, zoning and nuisance codes. Contact it before you sell so any open notice is known.

faqs.q: Why is my Parkersburg house taxed as non-residential?
faqs.a: West Virginia allows Class 2 residential status only for an owner occupied home with the owner's name on the deed. A house deeded to an LLC is taxed as Class 3 or 4, according to the Wood County Assessor.

faqs.q: When are Wood County property taxes due?
faqs.a: The first half is due September 1 and the second half March 1, with delinquency starting October 1 and April 1. Pay the Wood County Sheriff, not the Assessor.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Parkersburg house if I live out of state?
faqs.a: Yes. Title companies can handle signing by mail or remote notary. Confirm who is arranging the closing and how the deed will be recorded.
